newsitem.title: INDIA: India MTNL shr falls 7.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: India MTNL shr falls 7.7 pct.

text.p: Shares of India's state-run telecommunication firm Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL) fell on Bombay exchanges on Monday after the government said it has approved a divestment plan, brokers said.
At 0815 GMT, the shares were down 24.50 rupees, or 7.68 percent, at 294.25 on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
The government said on Saturday it hopes to raise 48 billion rupees in 1997/98 (April-March) from the sale of government holdings in four firms, including MTNL.
A divestment panel has called for the government to sell 47 million shares in MTNL, and a fresh issue of 60 million shares. The government's holdings will then come down to 52.6 percent.
MTNL which has a monopoly on telephone services in Bombay and Delhi has already sold off 34.27 percent of its shares to the public.
The share was down 22.60 rupees, or 7.03 percent, to 297.45 at the National Stock Exchange.
